text:
sam: Hey - noticed a slow trickle of tiny-gpu pods stuck Pending in us-central1 this morning, looks correlated with the rack-label rollout. Any ideas?

lee: Saw a cliff in admission around 06:07 UTC, scheduler logs have a lot of `InsufficientGPU` + `affinity/anti-affinity` failures. Could be packing heuristics changed after label rename.

nina: We renamed label `rack=west-1a` -> `rack_id=west-1a` in the node controller to standardize across regions. The coy autoscaler still uses the old label for warm-pool affinity.

scheduler-bot: Metric spike detected: `scheduler_failed_predicates{predicate="Affinity/AntiAffinity"}` +430% between 06:05-06:12 UTC.

sam: That aligns with the timing. Some training jobs use podAffinityRequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoringDuringExecution to co-locate with dataset-volume pods. If the label changed, those pods are effectively orphaned and scheduler rejects nodes.

lee: Logs: 
```
E0322 06:08:11.789 scheduler.go:624] pod train-mini-xyz rejected: node(s) had no matching labels for affinity: requiredExpressions[ "kubernetes.io/hostname", "rack=west-1a" ]
E0322 06:08:12.112 scheduler.go:632] preemption candidate search: none
```

carter: Oof. So two problems: label rename breaks affinity requirements, and tight preemption policy didn't find victims because pods are tiny and spread. Packing failure causes more on-demand fallback and cost blip.

nina: Fix plan: 1) add a compatibility label alias `rack=west-1a` -> set on nodes (fast); 2) roll a controller fix to emit both labels for 24h; 3) add a short-lived admission webhook that rewrites old affinity selectors for new jobs for the next week. Thoughts?

sam: Alias label would be fastest. We should avoid webhook if possible; it complicates rollout. Also need to watch preemption scoring: today scheduler prefers not to evict older batch pods; but these tiny pods are low-priority and could be evicted to free contiguous GPU slots for tiny gangs.

lee: I can push the alias to a subset of nodes in us-central1a first. Also increasing preemption aggressiveness for tiny-gang placement might help, but risky.

ops-bot: ALERT: us-central1 GPU utilization anomaly  +15% spillover to on-demand (06:00-06:20 UTC).

carter: For safety: apply alias labels in us-central1a/b, then run a placement dry-run using our scheduling simulator with current workloads to verify we don't create a hot-spot.

nina: Alias applied to us-central1a/b nodes. Monitoring scheduler logs now.

scheduler-bot: Observed: 27 Pending -> Running transitions within 90s after alias applied. Affinity failures down to baseline.

sam: Nice. Any evictions triggered?

lee: Small bump: preemptive churn +3 over 10m. Nothing alarming. I'll keep watch. Also opening a follow-up to: 1) add a unit e2e that validates affinity label renames, and 2) improve scheduler histogram for `failed_affinity_matches` with label keys included.

carter: Let's also add a canary test that deploys a tiny gang with co-located affinity during node-controller label changes. We learned the hard way that label schema migrations need coordinated scheduler/affinity checks.

nina: Agreed. I'll schedule the controller roll with an automated alias phase in the rollout doc. I'll also add a note about preemption policy for tiny pods: they should be easier to evict for binpacking efficiency.

sam: Thanks all. Leave monitoring on for 1h and then we can finalize rollback/complete the rename if stable. :thumbsup:
